voice.text: Two spoons. Same shape. [pause] Are they made of the same thing? Tap your guess.
Same object — a spoon. [pause] Different <emphasis>materials</emphasis>. One is wood. One is metal. [pause] The material is what it is made of.
One material makes many objects. [pause] Wood can be a spoon, a chair, a block — all wood!
Snip! Snip! Small pieces now. [pause] Are they still paper? <emphasis>Yes!</emphasis> [pause] Cutting changes the size — never the material.
The flashlight test! [pause] Glass: <emphasis>all</emphasis> the light goes through. [pause] Wax paper: only <emphasis>some</emphasis> light — a soft glow.
Wood: <emphasis>no</emphasis> light gets through. [pause] Now a thin ruler… still no light! [pause] Thin does not mean see-through.
Look at each thing. Tap the answer. [pause] The flashlight rounds ask: all, some, or none?
All nine tested! [pause] Now show what you know.
Not quite. Cutting only changes the size. [pause] Look — the pieces still look just the same inside.
Not quite. It is thin — but look behind it: shadow! [pause] Thin does not mean see-through.
Not quite. Look behind it — a soft glow. Not a bright spot, and not darkness. [pause] That is some light.
Not quite. Look closely: is it grainy wood, shiny metal, or see-through glass?
Not quite. Look at what happens behind the material, then try again.
Yes! [pause] Shiny and hard and cold — this spoon is metal.
Yes! [pause] You can see the wood grain — this chair is wood.
Yes! [pause] See-through and smooth — this cup is glass.
Yes! [pause] Smaller pieces — but every piece is still paper.
Yes! [pause] Half the size, same wax. Cutting never changes the material.
Yes! [pause] Glass lets all the light through — you can see right through it.
Yes! [pause] Wax paper lets some light through — a soft glow, no clear picture.
Yes! [pause] Wood blocks it all. No light gets through.
Yes! [pause] Even thin cardboard blocks all the light. Thin does not mean see-through!
A chair is made of wood. Which word is the material?
We cut a sheet of paper into little pieces. What are the little pieces?
We cut a wax candle in half. Is each half still wax?
A flashlight shines at window glass. How much light gets through?
A flashlight shines at a thin sheet of cardboard. How much light gets through?
<soft>You are a real material tester!</soft> [pause] Well done.
Good try! Let's watch the tester once more.
Lesson done! Now grab a real flashlight and test your house.
